description_short: Basic extraction of material–precursor–energy-source triplets from the ALE overview (Table I) to show how diverse ALE studies can be unified in a structured format.

paper.title: Atomic Layer Etching at the Tipping Point: An Overview

tables_modeled.label: Table I
tables_modeled.description: Summary of atomic layer etching (ALE) investigations, listing materials, adsorption precursor chemistries, and energy sources used for etching or desorption.

properties_used.label: material
properties_used.role: ALE substrate or film material summarized in Table I

properties_used.label: precursor chemistries for adsorption
properties_used.role: adsorption precursor chemistry used in the ALE cycle (e.g., Cl2, fluorocarbon species)

properties_used.label: energy source
properties_used.role: energy source or activation mode used for etching/desorption (e.g., ions, plasma, photons)

join_strategy.description: No cross-table joins are performed; this query operates on a single ORKG comparison that models Table I.
steps: Select all contributions (rows) from the ALE overview comparison (R1562672).
For each contribution, retrieve the material (P9071), precursor chemistry (P183142), and energy source (P183143) if present.
join_strategy.limitations: Some cells may be missing (e.g., no explicit energy source recorded), in which case the corresponding variable will be empty in the results.

aggregation_logic.description: This Easy Query does not aggregate or compute derived metrics.
details: Each row in the result corresponds directly to one ALE investigation as represented by a single comparison contribution.
Multiple investigations involving the same material but different precursors or energy sources will appear as separate rows, enabling later grouping or counting in downstream analyses.

output_shape.description: Simple triplet view of ALE studies from Table I.
columns: precursor: adsorption precursor chemistry used in the ALE cycle.
energy: energy source used for etching or desorption (e.g., plasma, ion bombardment, photon exposure).

postprocessing_notes.interpretation: The query provides a compact overview of how different ALE studies combine material systems, adsorption chemistries, and energy sources. This serves as a starting point for more advanced analyses, such as grouping by energy source, counting precursor usage across materials, or linking these process choices to etch rates and selectivities in subsequent queries.
